[2026-09-22] r:5283937055 review APPROVED by hebasto (member) (edited 2026-09-22):
ACK ce76c082cead6a107d1c95f584a0eff390b3539f, I have reviewed the code and it looks OK.

However, I'd like to leave a couple of thoughts regarding versioning of the Windows cross-build toolchain.

1. The MinGW-w64 version should be logged in the configure summary, along with the compiler version. See the proposal in #36029.

2. Historically, we were bound to whichever combination of MinGW-w64 and GCC a particular distribution shipped. Switching to Nix opens the door to testing every documented combination (with some patching).

    So I [tried](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin/actions/runs/35755777710/job/106841191753) MinGW-w64 12.0.0 + GCC 12.4.0:

    - The `wallet_migration.py` test [fails](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin/actions/runs/35755777710/job/106874712751). I haven't looked into it yet, but it may be a reason to bump the minimum supported MinGW-w64 version to 13.0, which contains many bug fixes.

    - Requiring GCC 13 or newer for the GUI appears unnecessary. Perhaps I misjudged the minimum toolchain requirements in 0a6724aaae973659b6c44eb5a062aaaaf57be870.
</new_statements>
